question: How can independently trained neural networks communicate through latent representations when their coordinate systems, dimensions, modalities, and available semantic correspondences differ?

key_findings.claim: The dissertation formalizes latent communication as recovering compatible views of an underlying semantic manifold despite unobservable, model-specific latent transformations.
key_findings.evidence: The problem statement separates input manifolds, encoder embeddings, unknown transformations, a semantic correspondence relation, and a universal or translated space. This unifies representation comparison, stitching, retrieval, and cross-modal alignment as instances of one problem.

key_findings.claim: Relative representations remove a known transformation class by encoding each sample through similarities to parallel anchor samples.
key_findings.evidence: If the chosen similarity is invariant to the latent transformation, independently trained encoders produce compatible anchor-relative coordinates. Experiments span word embeddings, image autoencoders, text classifiers, and vision transformers and permit zero-shot stitching without fitting an inter-model map.

key_findings.claim: When paired anchors are available, direct low-complexity translation—often approximately orthogonal after normalization—can outperform pure invariance while using relatively few correspondences.
key_findings.evidence: Affine, linear, least-squares orthogonal, and orthogonal maps are compared across architectures and modalities. Results show performance saturating with anchor count and often favoring orthogonal or affine translations, while scale normalization is essential for decoding.

key_findings.claim: Later chapters relax the strongest assumptions with products of invariances and bootstrapped anchors, and case studies extend the framework to frozen multimodal alignment, model aggregation, and zero-shot RL stitching.
key_findings.evidence: Multiple invariant projections improve communication when the transformation class is unknown; anchor optimization handles limited correspondences. Case studies align frozen vision/text encoders, aggregate heterogeneous models, and combine independently trained RL components without joint retraining.

key_findings.claim: Communication quality is conditional on anchor coverage and transformation assumptions, so zero-shot compatibility is not a universal property of independently trained networks.
key_findings.evidence: The author documents sensitivity to anchor cardinality and distribution, non-isometric relationships, architecture/task mismatch, dimensionality, and incomplete semantic correspondence, and calls for automatic transformation discovery and stronger theory.

method.core_idea: Make latent representations interoperable either by quotienting out nuisance transformations with anchor-relative coordinates or by estimating a constrained map from semantic anchors.
method.mechanism: The thesis defines the latent communication problem, constructs relative encodings from similarities to corresponding anchors, compares direct affine/linear/orthogonal translations, composes several invariance families when the nuisance class is unknown, optimizes scarce anchors, and applies the resulting interfaces to frozen-model stitching across tasks and modalities.
assumptions: The compared latent spaces encode a shared semantic manifold with sufficient overlap.
Available anchors are correctly paired and cover the geometry needed at test time.
Nuisance transformations lie in or near the invariance/translation family chosen by the method.
Downstream decoders remain valid when fed a communicated representation after normalization.
Task performance is an adequate test of semantic alignment even when several transformations yield comparable predictions.

techniques.role: Maps absolute coordinates to similarities with shared semantic reference points.
Estimates affine, linear, or orthogonal maps from paired anchors.
Concatenates or combines projections robust to several possible nuisance transformations.
Optimizes or expands limited semantic correspondences.
Tests whether a frozen encoder can drive another model's frozen decoder or policy component.

evaluations.setting: Independent word embeddings, image autoencoders, text classifiers, and vision models with parallel anchors.
evaluations.metric: Representation similarity, reconstruction, classification F1/accuracy, and stitched task performance.
evaluations.result: Relative coordinates substantially improve cross-model compatibility and enable several zero-shot stitches that fail in absolute coordinates.
evaluations.baseline: Raw absolute representations, CKA-style similarity, and trained stitching layers where applicable.

evaluations.setting: Cross-architecture and cross-modal direct translation with varying anchor count.
evaluations.metric: Reconstruction error, classification accuracy, retrieval, and generation quality proxies.
evaluations.result: Simple orthogonal or affine maps often recover useful compatibility and saturate with a modest number of well-distributed anchors; scale correction is critical.
evaluations.baseline: Linear, affine, least-squares orthogonal, and strict orthogonal translation families plus no alignment.

evaluations.setting: Unknown-transformation experiments across vision, text, and graph encoders.
evaluations.metric: Zero-shot stitching accuracy after individual versus combined invariant projections.
evaluations.result: A product of invariances is more robust across heterogeneous model pairs than committing to one transformation assumption, at increased representation dimension.
evaluations.baseline: Single-invariance relative representations and learned direct translations.

evaluations.setting: Frozen multimodal alignment, latent ensemble aggregation, and reinforcement-learning component stitching.
evaluations.metric: Retrieval/classification and task reward or policy performance without joint retraining.
evaluations.result: The case studies demonstrate nontrivial communication, but each relies on task-specific anchor construction and does not establish universal plug-and-play interoperability.
evaluations.baseline: Unaligned frozen components and jointly trained/task-specific interfaces where reported.

limitations: Shared semantic content and trustworthy paired anchors are prerequisites, even in the nominally zero-shot settings.
Relative coordinates scale in dimension and compute with the anchor set unless compressed.
Invariance can discard task-relevant information if the assumed nuisance transformation is actually semantic.
Results cover many small or medium models and case studies but not frontier-scale language-model activation exchange.
The dissertation consolidates several authored works, so protocols and baselines vary between chapters.
failure_modes: Anchors concentrated in one semantic region can align locally while distorting out-of-region samples.
Incorrect correspondences can systematically rotate or warp the communicated space.
A non-isometric nonlinear relationship can defeat cosine-relative and orthogonal translation methods.
A receiving decoder can exploit model-specific latent details that are absent from a semantically aligned but compressed interface.
reusable_insights: Anchor-relative coordinates turn a representation-alignment problem into the design of an invariant similarity function.
Transformation-family selection should be validated by downstream stitching, not only representational correlation.
Anchor diversity matters more than raw anchor count once the relevant manifold directions are covered.
Combining several cheap invariances is a robust fallback when the latent nuisance class is unknown.
open_questions: Can anchors and transformation families be discovered without paired data or downstream labels?
How should latent communication preserve uncertainty, causality, and rare semantic directions?
Can standardized latent interfaces support modular RL or language systems across independently trained foundation models?
What privacy leakage is introduced when anchor similarities expose a frozen model's internal geometry?

competitive_landscape.title: Relative representations enable zero-shot latent space communication
competitive_landscape.relationship: Presents the anchor-relative representation method that forms a central chapter and foundation of the dissertation.
competitive_landscape.difference: The paper focuses on the core zero-shot construction; the thesis unifies it with direct translation, unknown-transform products, scarce-anchor methods, and broader case studies.

competitive_landscape.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses simple learned stitching layers to test functional compatibility between frozen model representations.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns a task interface between two models; latent communication aims for zero- or low-fit alignment through anchors and transformation invariance across dimensions and modalities.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.relationship: Aligns independently trained networks by resolving hidden-unit permutation symmetries before weight-space merging.
competitive_landscape.difference: Git Re-Basin acts on parameters of architecture-compatible models; this thesis aligns activation spaces and supports cross-architecture, cross-dimension, and cross-modal communication.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The dissertation establishes latent communication as a unified research problem and develops a family of relative, translated, and anchor-bootstrapped solutions across modalities and tasks.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Formalization, multiple method chapters, extensive cross-model experiments, and RL/multimodal case studies connect previously separate representation-similarity and stitching questions.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The unified framework and systematic relaxation of assumptions are the main contribution; success remains conditional on semantic overlap, anchor quality, and a tractable nuisance-transformation family.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 134-page extraction, with emphasis on formalization, methods, case studies, limitations, and anchor appendices. Primary alignment and stitching competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
